terms.gloss: what someone has said, a statement
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.23: dictōrum conventōrumque cōnstantia et vēritās
terms.comment: Latin often names a statement by what was said: quod dīcis, “what you say”.

evidence: Cic. Off. 3.104: est enim jūs jūrandum affirmātiō religiōsa

terms.gloss: a statement in logic, a proposition
evidence: Cic. Tusc. 1.14: id ergō est prōnūntiātum, quod est vērum aut falsum
terms.comment: Cicero’s rendering of Greek ἀξίωμα, made up on the spot (“so it occurs to me to call it for now”); a term of philosophy.

phrases.latin: id ergō est prōnūntiātum, quod est vērum aut falsum
phrases.english: a statement, then, is whatever is either true or false

phrases.latin: est enim jūs jūrandum affirmātiō religiōsa
phrases.english: for an oath is a statement made under religious sanction

sources: Lewis & Short: dictum · Lewis & Short: affirmatio · Lewis & Short: pronuntiatum
Cic. Off. 1.23 and 3.104, Tusc. 1.14 checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).
